# Best open-ear earbuds for running

I can't browse, so these picks come from the search results. The review pages below carry the retailer buy buttons. I only have a direct purchase link for one product (the AeroFit 2).

## Top picks

**Best overall: Bose Ultra Open Earbuds (about $199, list $299)**
- Runner's World ranks it best overall, praising the sound quality, the comfortable clip design, and a fit that doesn't bounce.
- WIRED likes the physical buttons, which are easier to use mid-run than touch controls.
- Drawbacks: about 7 hours per battery, an IPX4 rating (weak for heavy rain), and the price.
- Runner's World says Bose plans a new open-ear pair within a month, so you may want to wait for it.
- [Runner's World guide](https://www.runnersworld.com/gear/g63667125/best-open-ear-headphones-for-running/) · [WIRED guide](https://www.wired.com/story/best-open-earbuds/)

**Best bone conduction: Shokz OpenRun Pro 2 (list $180, listed at $125 at some retailers)**
- It keeps your ears the most open, which matters for road running.
- It has 12 hours of battery, IP55 water resistance, and physical buttons.
- WIRED rates it 8/10 for running, with bigger bass than the previous generation but somewhat less clarity.
- It can clash with long hair, high ponytails, and winter hats.
- [WIRED review](https://www.wired.com/review/review-shokz-openrun-pro-2/) · [RTINGS comparison with the Bose](https://www.rtings.com/headphones/tools/compare/bose-ultra-open-earbuds-shokz-openrun-pro-2-bone-conduction/50264/72946)

**Best for long runs: Shokz OpenDots 2 ($200)**
- It gets 10 hours per charge (40 with the case) and has an IP57 rating.
- WIRED's top pick overall.
- [WIRED guide](https://www.wired.com/story/best-open-earbuds/)

**Best value for runners: Nothing Ear (Open) (about $99 at Amazon, list $149)**
- SoundGuys calls it the best workout earbud for running.
- It has an IP54 rating and strong bass for an open-ear design.
- [SoundGuys open-ear guide](https://www.soundguys.com/best-open-ear-headphones-and-earbuds-115102/) · [SoundGuys workout guide](https://www.soundguys.com/best-workout-earbuds-2719/)

## Budget options

- **Soundcore AeroFit 2:** It's an ear-hook design with IP55 and 10 hours per charge (42 with the case). [Buy at Soundcore](https://dealectric.com/go/soundcore-aerofit-2). This is an affiliate link from Dealectric, which earns a commission at no cost to you.
  - Prices conflict between sources. Dealectric lists $129.99 and says code AFSC20 takes it to about $104. SoundGuys lists an MSRP of $99.99 and $79.99 at Amazon. Check the current price at checkout before paying.
  - [Dealectric listing](https://dealectric.com/soundcore-aerofit-2) · [SoundGuys](https://www.soundguys.com/best-open-ear-headphones-and-earbuds-115102/)
- **JLab Flex Open (about $40–50):** Runner's World's budget pick. The sound is thinner than on pricier pairs, but it's a low-risk way to see if you like clip-ons. [Runner's World](https://www.runnersworld.com/gear/g63667125/best-open-ear-headphones-for-running/)
- **Soundpeats PearlClip Pro ($50):** WIRED's cheap pick, with IPX5 and 7.5 hours per charge. [WIRED](https://www.wired.com/story/best-open-earbuds/)

## Quick advice
- If you run in heavy rain or sweat a lot, choose the OpenRun Pro 2 or OpenDots 2.
- If you want the best sound, choose the Bose.
- If you wear glasses, hats, or have long hair, a clip-on or ear-hook design is usually easier than a neckband.
- Open-ear designs leak sound and don't block noise. Keep the volume low enough to hear traffic.

I can narrow this down if you tell me your budget, whether you use an iPhone or Android, and whether you run mostly on roads or in the gym.
